notes: Quoted-string, domain-literal and obsolete forms are not modeled by the cases.

statement: addr-spec is local-part "@" domain; local-part is dot-atom, quoted-string or obs-local-part; domain is dot-atom, domain-literal or obs-domain.
inference: A plain mailbox has exactly one separating at sign between a local part and a domain.

notes: The inference concerns the dot-atom form only; quoted-string local parts are out of scope.

statement: dot-atom-text is 1*atext *("." 1*atext); atext is ALPHA, DIGIT and the characters ! # $ % & ' * + - / = ? ^ _ ` { | } ~.
inference: In the dot-atom form a local part cannot start or end with a dot or contain two consecutive dots, and a plus sign is an ordinary atext character.

notes: The limits were read through a section summary; the exact normative wording was not re-read.

statement: Size limits for SMTP: a local-part is at most 64 octets, a domain at most 255 octets and a path at most 256 octets.
inference: A mailbox whose local part exceeds 64 octets is not a deliverable SMTP address; RFC 5322 itself states no such limit, so the limit is transport-level.

statement: example.com, example.net and example.org are reserved second-level domain names for documentation and examples.
location: Section 3, Reserved Example Second Level Domain Names
inference: Addresses under these domains cannot belong to a person and are safe public values.

statement: The top-level names .test, .example, .invalid and .localhost are reserved; .invalid is intended for names that are obviously invalid.
location: Section 2, TLDs for Testing, & Documentation Examples
inference: An address at a reserved top-level name has no deliverable mailbox by construction.

statement: The names test, example and invalid, and example.com, example.net and example.org, are registered as special-use domain names.
